title: Forensic-proof guide: customer-managed networking
content:
Purpose
---
This doc sketches a lightweight, tamper-resistant evidence bundle and sampling policy for customer-managed networking changes in Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Goal: give operators + customers a clear, scripted way to capture the ‘what, who, when, why’ for network changes so audits and incident forensics are reproducible without creating heavy ops burden.

Context / why now
- Multiple pilot customers have asked for a compact export that their auditors can consume; they want deterministic proofs rather than big raw pcap dumps.
- We need a single interoperable format that: supports operator attestation, includes cryptographic receipts (signatures), and is easy to attach to approval gates and the control-plane audit store.
- Related: ties into the global approval-gates effort (see ENG-1428) and the approval-sampling experiments Leah ran in Q2.

Non-goals
- This is not a full SIEM product. We won’t attempt to ingest customers’ internal logs or replace their forensic tooling.
- Not aiming to capture packet-level DPI or payloads. Focus on metadata + flow summaries + control-plane events.

High-level design summary
- Evidence bundle concept: a zip-like archive ("evidence-bundle.v1.zip") containing a human-readable manifest, compact event logs (JSONL), deterministic flow digests, operator attestation token, and optional customer-supplied artifacts (screenshots, ticket links).
- Immutable manifest: lists bundle contents and SHA256 for each file, with timestamp and monotonic bundle-id. Manifest also references the approval gate id and the change-id (if available).
- Signing model: control-plane produces a server-sig (Ed25519) over the manifest; operator can attach an operator-sig (also Ed25519). If customer-side signing is enabled, they can add a customer-sig. Signatures recorded in a small verification.json file.
- Sampling & retention: lightweight sampling policy stores full bundles for 10% of non-critical changes and 100% for changes hitting a gated approval path. All bundles subject to retention rules (90 days default, configurable per-customer).

User stories
- As a Platform Operator, I want to export a verifiable evidence bundle after approving a customer VPC change so security ops can review it later.
- As a Customer Auditor, I want to validate that the bundle was produced by Redwood’s control-plane and signed by the operator who approved the change.
- As an Incident Responder, I want quick-flow digests so I can triage whether a network change likely caused an SLA breach.

Requirements (functional)
- R1: Bundle must contain manifest.json (SHA256 checksums), events.jsonl (chronological control-plane events), flow-digest.json (compact per-flow metadata), verification.json (signatures), and metadata.txt (human notes).
- R2: Each bundle assigned a unique bundle-id that is monotonically increasing per-customer and referenced in control-plane traces and the approval audit log.
- R3: System must attach bundle-id to approval-gate records and make it queryable from Console and the audit API.
- R4: Signing keys are customer-aware: server-sig uses control-plane key; operator-sig uses operator's keyvault reference. Key rotation must be handled; verification.json must include key id and key rotation epoch.
- R5: Export API: POST /v1/customers/{id}/evidence-bundles with params: change_id, include_customer_artifacts (bool), sampling_override (enum: force, skip, auto).
- R6: Verify tool: CLI or API that fetches a bundle and returns verification status and a short human report.

Requirements (non-functional)
- NF1: Bundle generation should add <200ms median latency to approval flow when sampling_override=auto (not forced).
- NF2: Archive format must be stable across versions; version string in manifest required.
- NF3: Typical bundle size target: <5MB for common control-plane-only bundles; allow larger for attachments but warn in Console.

Evidence format details (working sketch)
- manifest.json (object): bundle_id, created_at, version, files: [{path, sha256, size_bytes}], approval_gate_id, change_id, operator_id, region.
- events.jsonl: one JSON per line; include event_type, timestamp, actor, event_payload (small).
- flow-digest.json: array of objects with src_cidr, dst_cidr, service_ports, action, pre_change_hash, post_change_hash (hashes over routing/ACL sets).
- verification.json: server_sig: {key_id, sig, algo}, operator_sigs: [{operator_id, key_id, sig}], customer_sigs: optional.
- metadata.txt: freeform notes from operator (why approved, rollback notes).

Approval gate integration notes
- When an approval gate is satisfied, the gate handler shall call evidence-bundler with change context. If sampling decides to produce a full bundle, bundler returns a bundle_id and stores the archive in customer-scoped evidence storage (S3 or on-prem store).
- Approval gates must display 'Bundle produced: id' inline and link to the Console evidence viewer. If sampling skipped, show indicator 'No bundle (sampling)'.

Sampling policy (detailed)
- Default: auto-sample: 10% of operator-approved changes; 100% of changes that touch high-sensitivity ACLs or cross-account peering.
- Forced sampling: policy can be overridden by operator or customer via API (sampling_override param). Forced bundles are logged and audited.
- Deterministic sample selection: use change_id hashed with day-seed to generate reproducible sampling decisions (helps avoid bias and makes audits explainable).

Retention & storage
- Default retention: 90 days for sampled bundles, configurable per-customer up to 1 year for enterprise contracts.
- Storage: customer-scoped S3 prefix with SSE-KMS; for on-prem installations, evidence_store.adrs points to local object store. Control-plane retains only the manifest index and minimal metadata for search after bundle retention expires (index TTL policy).

Forensic replay & triage
- Provide a small script (bundler-verify) that unpacks bundle, verifies checksums and signatures, and produces a short triage summary: changed resources, pre/post hashes, impacted flows.
- For deep investigations, link to a customer-provided forensic playbook location (customers should supply additional internal logs for packet-level work).

Console & API UX
- Console: Evidence viewer shows manifest, timeline (events.jsonl), operator notes, and quick-verify status. Allow download of bundle and copy of verification report.
- API: GET /v1/customers/{id}/evidence-bundles?from=&to=&change_id= returns list of bundles. GET /v1/customers/{id}/evidence-bundles/{bundle_id} returns pre-signed download link and verification summary.

Operator workflow (example)
- Operator opens change ticket -> inspects diff -> approves via Console -> Console triggers approval-gate -> bundler decision -> if bundle created, attach id in ticket and email to customer contact.

Security considerations
- Keys: private signing keys must live in HSM/KMS; operator-sig performed via ephemeral auth token tied to operator session.
- Tamper evidence: manifest+signatures + checksum prevents silent edits; store verification results as immutable entries in the control-plane audit log (append-only).

Open questions / TODOs
- Q1: Should we allow redactable bundles where customers can request PII redaction before export? (privacy teams to weigh in)
- Q2: How to handle multi-operator approvals (n of m signatures)? Design needs to support threshold signatures or simply store multiple operator-sigs.
- Q3: Retention SLAs and legal hold mechanics for customer subpoenas.
- TODO: wire up sample selection experiment (A/B) with telemetry bucket SR-2374.

Next steps (short-term)
- Spike: implement proof-of-concept bundler prototype that outputs manifest + verification.json (owner: Jonah, 2 weeks).
- UX: design Console evidence viewer mockups (owner: Priya, mock by 2025-11-20).
- Infra: storage config options for on-prem (Marco to prototype mount).
- Legal & Compliance consult: finalize retention defaults and redaction policy (Lena will schedule).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally pragmatic — we prefer a small interoperable artifact to huge raw logs. Looking for feedback on the manifest shape and sampling heuristics.
- If you know of regulatory constraints for Germany/Austria on exportable signed artifacts, flag them here.

References
- internal: CON-priv-deploy-evidence-design (Confluence), ENG-1428, SR-2374.
- external: suggestions from customer audit teams — sample format inspired by forensic manifests used at BigCo X.

Changelog

- 2025-11-08: added signing model and API sketch (Jonah)
- 2025-11-12: clarified sampling policy and retention defaults (Priya)
